Subject: Infra choice & HIPAA evidence — next steps (MedScope)

Hi Claire,

Thanks again for the productive conversation earlier this morning. Quick recap from Redwood + the clarifying questions we need to finalize a recommended hosting path for MedScope: 

- Use case & constraints we heard:
  • Processing PHI (clinical notes and lab results) — must be covered by a BAA
  • Audit window: external audit planned for late June; they may request logs going back 12 months
  • Security gates: SOC 2 Type II report, pen test summary, and KMS integration required

- Hosting tradeoffs (high level):
  • Hosted API (fastest): possible if BAA accepted and strict ingestion/retention controls applied; fits small-to-medium scale but shared tenancy increases noise in network traces for auditors
  • Dedicated (recommended middle path): dedicated GPU pools + VPC peering; gives isolation, predictable throughput, and we can provide audit logs and KMS options — typically the best balance
  • Private/VPC-on-prem (maximum isolation): recommended if MedScope requires complete network isolation or local-only processing

Clarifying questions to confirm call-to-action:
1) Expected sustained QPS and peak tokens per minute (rough numbers suffice)
2) Data retention requirement (you mentioned ~6 months on the call; is 180 days final?)
3) Do you require customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS/HSM) with separate key material?
4) Will MedScope accept a Redwood-hosted BAA + SOC2 artifacts, or do procurement/legal prefer Dedicated/Private for the contract?
5) Primary procurement contact and timeline (PO/contract lead)

Attachments: call-notes.pdf (short summary), redwood_hipaa-options-1pager.pdf

If you can reply with the quick answers above, I’ll assemble a short decision matrix and a recommended plan (including list of evidence we can provide) and propose dates for a technical deep-dive.

Best,
Irene Choi
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
irene@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0126

From: Claire Young <claire.young@medscope.com>

Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 12:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Infra choice & HIPAA evidence — next steps (MedScope)

Hi Irene,

Great summary — thanks. Answers below and I’ve attached our security requirements spreadsheet (medscope_security_requirements.xlsx).

1) Throughput: Pilot expected to be light — ~10–25 requests/sec sustained, peaks up to ~80 req/sec. Token sizes small (200–400 tokens per request).
2) Retention: We need 180 days for operational data; audit may request access to 12 months of logs. We prefer configurable retention windows.
3) KMS: Yes — we require customer-managed AWS KMS keys (MedScope controls key material).
4) Contract/legal: Procurement prefers Dedicated or Private for PHI if the vendor cannot guarantee tenant-level separation and KMS control. They will consider hosted + BAA only if the hosted environment supports customer-managed KMS and dedicated network paths.
5) Procurement contact: procurement@medscope.com (Sally Park). Decision target: May 15 for go/no-go; pilot target: June 15.

Also: please include SOC2 Type II report and pen test summary with the evidence package. Jared and I will review the tech deep-dive after we see the docs.

Thanks,
Claire
Director of Platform Security | MedScope Health
claire.young@medscope.com

Hi team,

Thanks for the context. Based on MedScope’s answers, here’s my recommended approach and an evidence checklist we can realistically provide by April 15: 

Recommendation (short):
- Primary recommendation: Redwood Dedicated with VPC peering + support for customer-managed AWS KMS. Dedicated gives the isolation procurement prefers while allowing us to provide audit logs and predictable performance.
- If customer requires their own local infrastructure or a fully air-gapped environment, recommend Redwood Private (on-prem package) — higher lead time (~8–12 weeks) and additional procurement terms.

Why Dedicated fits:
- Supports VPC peering and controlled egress (network diagrams can show separation)
- We support customer-managed KMS; we can provide a KMS integration guide and an ops checklist for key rotation and access controls
- Audit artifacts (SOC2 Type II, pen test summary, control matrix) are readily shareable under NDA/BAA

Evidence we will deliver by Apr 15:
1) SOC2 Type II report (redwood_soc2_summary.pdf) — redacted as needed
2) Pen test summary (redwood_pen_test_summary.pdf)
3) KMS integration guide and ops checklist (redwood_kms_integration.docx)
4) Network diagram showing VPC peering and egress controls
5) Retention & logging matrix + sample audit logs (configurable retention to meet 180 day and 12 month audit requests)
6) BAA draft for review (we’ll share legal contact and an initial draft)

Proposed next steps and owners:
- Irene: coordinate procurement intro to Sally Park (procurement@medscope.com) and schedule legal loop-in (by Mar 29)
- Marissa: produce network diagram + retention/logging matrix (by Apr 5)
- Karthik (me): prepare SOC2 + pen test artifacts and KMS guide (by Apr 12)
- Sales/SE deep-dive: propose 1-hour technical review (options Apr 6–8). Karthik + Marissa + Irene to attend.

If MedScope confirms Dedicated is acceptable, we’ll scope a short pilot (Dedicated capacity with limited pool) to hit their June 15 pilot target. If they insist on Private, we should flag the longer lead time immediately.

Claire/Jared — happy to set up the technical review once you confirm best times next week.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
